name: Sender Address & Domain Mismatch
description: The sender's display name claims to be official (e.g. 'Campus IT Support'), but the actual email address or root domain is unrelated, external, or misspelled (e.g., '@campus-helpdesk.test' instead of '@campus.edu').
guidance: Expand the sender header in your email client to examine the exact domain after the '@' sign.

name: Unusual Urgency, Panic, or Ultimatums
description: The message demands immediate action within 12, 24, or 48 hours, threatening account closure, course deregistration, legal action, or missed monetary prizes if you do not comply immediately.
guidance: Legitimate academic and institutional departments provide ample notice and structured escalation processes before taking punitive actions.

name: Unexpected or Suspicious Attachments
description: Unsolicited archives (.zip, .rar), executable files (.exe, .scr, .vbs), or Office documents (.docm, .xlsm) that prompt you to 'Enable Editing' or 'Enable Macros'.
guidance: Never open unexpected files or enable active macros. Verify with the sender via a separate, trusted channel first.

name: Requests for Passwords, PINs, or One-Time Passcodes (OTP)
description: The message explicitly asks you to reply with your password, enter it into a web form, or provide the 2-Factor Authentication (MFA) SMS code sent to your phone.
guidance: Real IT departments and financial institutions will NEVER ask for your password or one-time passcodes under any circumstances.

name: Unusual Payment Requests or Overpayment Schemes
description: Demands for unexpected fee settlements, wire transfers, Zelle/Venmo payments, cryptocurrency, gift cards, or requests to deposit a check and transfer a portion to a third party.
guidance: Campus billing operates through official university financial ledgers. Advance fee requirements and gift card payment requests are universal hallmarks of fraud.

name: Suspicious Links or Mismatched Anchor Domains
description: Hyperlinked text showing one official address while the actual destination URL points to a different domain, an IP address, a URL shortener (bit.ly), or an unusual TLD (.xyz, .top, .buzz).
guidance: Hover over hyperlinks without clicking to inspect the real URL destination in your browser's bottom status bar.

name: Grammar, Punctuation, or Formatting Inconsistencies
description: Awkward phrasings, unnatural grammar, garbled character sets, poor logo resolution, mixed typography, or misspellings of institutional department names.
guidance: While modern AI has reduced obvious spelling errors, awkward sentence structures and inconsistent formatting still frequently indicate counterfeit templates.

name: Requests to Bypass Normal Institutional Procedures
description: Instructions to bypass established university procurement channels, keep the communication confidential from professors or advisors, or communicate exclusively via personal email/messaging apps.
guidance: Legitimate institutional leaders respect official channels and policies. Pressure to bypass standard oversight is a major indicator of spear phishing or BEC.
